doc.title: Joe Muranyi interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2007

chapter: Childhood in Ohio and first music
title: Gypsy band bass players and Cutty Cutshall
summary: He loved the bass player in the Hungarian gypsy bands and finds that trombonist Cutty Cutshall shared the same fondness.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Um, they really grab it. © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-
Yeah. Zoom — zoom — zoom. And I’d just stand in front of them and I enjoyed that so much. And I’ll tell you there’s a funny thing. You ever hear of a trombone player named Cutty Cutshall?

I knew Cutty. I played with him you know, more than a few times at the Eddie Condon’s in midtown in the 50s. And somehow we got onto this. And it turns out he was from eastern Pennsylvania or something like that, you know I was born in Martin’s Ferry, which is on the Ohio River down the river from Pittsburgh a hundred miles or not even that. And he was from that area, and he too, even though he didn’t have the Hungarian background, he too loved the gypsy bands and the bass player going zoom — zoom — zoom. So it was a funny kind of thing.
